fixes.problem: The r9 crowd fix landed (hero walkers 2 -> 8), but S.topUp drops walkers on the few eq waypoints inside the view cone (eq loop step 14 m, all on one line 6 m inset from SHORE_N) with only +-1.5 m jitter and no separation test. Result: hero_noon has 4 bodies inside ~1.2 m (pink shirt walks through green shirt, a third behind them), hero has the grey-top and blue-shirt walkers overlapping and a pink walker standing inside the bench footprint line, hero_night the same 5-body knot, phone_hud a knot right of the player. The knot sits at x 0.55-0.65, so it competes with the player and reads as a spawn bug, not a lived-in promenade.
fixes.fix: peds.js S.topUp: (1) build candidates as points, not waypoints: for each eq/landing waypoint in view take 3 offsets along the local shore normal at inset 2.5, 6 and 10 m (normal = perpendicular of w[i+1]-w[i-1]) plus +-4 m along the loop. (2) Reject a candidate within 3.5 m of any walker already placed or in view, within 4 m of the player, or within 1.2 m of a bench (props bench points). (3) Spread by depth: bins 8-20, 20-35, 35-55 m, at most ceil(want/3) per bin. (4) Give each placed walker a random dir (+-1), cruise in its range, and offset the clip time by Math.random()*clipDuration so neighbours never step in phase. Apply the same 3.5 m rejection in S.prime (jitter +-1 m currently).

fixes.problem: hero shaded pavers sample 33,32,42 (luma ~33; r8 36,31,32): the hue is fixed (no more maroon) but the level is not. env 1.35 -> 1.6 at el 8 landed and luma_p5 stayed 26. fixes.area: shadow split tone reads violet (asphalt, footpaths, shade)
fixes.problem: The road tint fix landed (world/index.js road setRGB(1.85,1.72,1.52), env 0.55) yet street_sgt road is 46,53,71 and shops 49,56,73 (B-R +25, unchanged). Cause found: the grade's splitShadow [0.89,0.98,1.13] (art.js) is applied at full weight to everything below linear luma 0.05 (shaders.js line 519, smoothstep(0.05,0.65,ls)), i.e. every road, footpath and shade pixel; R and G drop together and B rises, which is violet, not the bible's teal (#2E4560 has G > R). Same cause for the blue-violet footpath tiles in shops and the blue cast on the parked cars in street_sgt (27,37,57).
fixes.fix: art.js grade.splitShadow [0.89,0.98,1.13] -> [0.90,1.02,1.06] (teal: G up, B less). shaders.js line 519: weight the split by saturation guard so neutral greys keep their hue: t *= mix(uSplitS, uSplitH, smoothstep(0.05,0.65,ls)) -> t *= mix(mix(vec3(1.0), uSplitS, 0.75), uSplitH, smoothstep(0.03,0.65,ls)).

fixes.area: golden sky above the horizon stays mauve-grey

The visible band (0-24 deg up at pitch -7, vfov 62) is dominated by the horizon colour: sky.js hgt = 1 - exp(-up * 4.2) is only 0.66 at 15 deg, and the sqrt-space mix with the warm, az-boosted horizon gives lilac. fixes.fix: sky.js line ~93: float hgt = 1.0 - exp(-up * mix(4.2, 6.5, sunset)); so at low sun the blue arrives by ~10 deg while the amber stays in a low band; horizon az boost mix(0.6,1.2,...) -> mix(0.5,1.25,...) to keep the hot side warm and the anti-sun side cooler.
